mainTopic: Laws of buildings and stones used for עבודה זרה: the fallen wall, טומאה of its materials, and the three kinds of houses and stones
overview: This amud opens at the end of a משנה about a wall next to a house of עבודה זרה. If the wall was shared, it is treated as half and half. The stones, wood and dust are טמא like a שרץ, but רבי עקיבא says they are טמא like a נדה, so they make a person טמא even by carrying. The גמרא asks whether pulling the wall back gives the idol extra space. It answers that the space becomes a bathroom, and after some back-and-forth about privacy it settles on a bathroom for children. It also gives a second answer: he fences the space off with thorns. Next, a new משנה lists three kinds of houses: built for עבודה זרה, plastered for it, or one an idol was only brought into. רב adds that bowing to a house also forbids it, and the משנה still counts three because building and bowing are cancelled the same way. A parallel משנה lists three kinds of stones. The גמרא finally reads רבי אמי's statement as teaching that even plaster worked into a stone can be removed to permit it.

steps.title: A shared wall is split half and half
steps.stepSummary: If the fallen wall belonged to both him and the house of עבודה זרה, it is treated as half his and half theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is judged as half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its rule about a fallen wall. If the wall was jointly owned by the person and the house of עבודה זרה, the space is treated as half his and half theirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule was that he pulls back four אמות into his own property before rebuilding. For a shared wall, the measurement starts from the middle of the wall's space, since only half of it was his. So he only has to pull back from his half.

phrases.english: It is judged as half and half.
phrases.notes: This is talking about a wall that belonged half to him and half to the house of עבודה זרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's earlier rule (before this section) about pulling back four אמות before rebuilding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall shared with a house of עבודה זרה is treated as half belonging to each side.

steps.title: The materials are impure like a creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The stones, wood and dust of the house of עבודה זרה are טמא like a שרץ, learned from ״שַׁקֵּץ תְּשַׁקְּצֶנּוּ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its stones, its wood and its dust make things impure like a creeping animal, as it says: 'You shall utterly detest it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches a new rule about טומאה. The building materials of a house of עבודה זרה make a person טמא the way a שרץ does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a word link. The פסוק about עבודה זרה uses the word ״שַׁקֵּץ״, and the תורה uses a similar word, שֶׁקֶץ, for creeping animals. So the טומאה of עבודה זרה is like a שרץ. That means it makes things טמא by touching, but not by carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: a creeping animal, which is טמא by touch
'You shall utterly detest it,' the פסוק about עבודה זרה
as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: Its stones, its wood and its dust
make impure like a creeping animal,
as it is said: 'You shall utterly detest it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of rebuilding the wall to the טומאה of the materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The materials of a house of עבודה זרה are טמא like a שרץ, based on ״שַׁקֵּץ תְּשַׁקְּצֶנּוּ״.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: impure like a menstruating woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא compares עבודה זרה to a נדה, so it also makes a person טמא by carrying (משא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: like a menstruating woman, as it says: 'You will cast them away like a menstruating woman; Go away, you will say to it.' Just as a menstruating woman makes impure by carrying, so too עבודה זרה makes impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with the first opinion. He says the טומאה of עבודה זרה is like that of a נדה, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical difference between the opinions is carrying. A שרץ only makes someone טמא by touch. A נדה also makes someone טמא if he carries or moves her, even without touching. So according to רבי עקיבא, carrying an item of עבודה זרה also makes a person טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: one who is unwell, used here for a נדה
carrying, which makes a person טמא even without touching
'just as... so too...', a comparison formula

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that the materials are טמא. They argue only about which kind of טומאה it is: like a שרץ (touch only) or like a נדה (touch and carrying).

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: like a menstruating woman,
as it is said: 'You will cast them away like a menstruating woman;
Go away, you will say to it,'
just as a menstruating woman makes impure by carrying,
so too idol worship makes impure by carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the previous opinion about which kind of טומאה applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, עבודה זרה is טמא like a נדה and makes a person טמא even by carrying.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree the materials are טמא. רבי עקיבא (נדה) adds carrying, while the first opinion (שרץ) is touch only.

steps.title: Isn't he giving more space to the idol?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: pulling the wall back leaves extra open space for the עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But he is creating more space for the idol worship!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule about pulling the wall four אמות into his own property. It challenges that rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he builds his wall further back, the gap between him and the house of עבודה זרה gets bigger. That open area could end up serving the idol and give it more room. The rule meant to distance him from עבודה זרה seems to end up helping it.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ וְהָא קָא מַרְוַוח לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה!
phrases.english: גמרא: But he is creating more space for the idol worship!
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה's rule that he pulls back four אמות into his own land before rebuilding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back past the טומאה rules to question the wall-rebuilding rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's instruction to pull back four אמות before rebuilding.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaving an empty gap gives the עבודה זרה more usable space, which defeats the purpose of distancing from it.

steps.title: He turns the space into a bathroom
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא מסורא answers that he uses the empty space as a bathroom, so it does not benefit the idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא from סורא said: He makes it into a bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא מסורא answers the challenge. The person turns the gap into a bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the space is a bathroom, it is degraded and cannot serve as honorable extra room for the עבודה זרה. So pulling the wall back does not help the idol at all. The משנה's rule stands.

phrases.english: רב חנינא from סורא said:
He makes it into a bathroom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: דְּעָבֵד לֵיהּ בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the rule is carried out in practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pulling back the wall leaves open space that benefits the עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The space is made into a bathroom, so it brings no honor or benefit to the עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A bathroom needs privacy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the bathroom answer: a bathroom must be private, but this open space is not enclosed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a bathroom needs privacy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of רב חנינא מסורא from step 5. A bathroom has to be a private place, and this open space does not seem private.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not let him build a wall in that space, so it stays open and anyone could see in. A bathroom is supposed to be hidden for צניעות. So how can this open space be used as a bathroom?

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, an opening word for a challenge

phrases.english: But it needs privacy!
phrases.notes: "It" is the bathroom from the last answer. He can't build a wall in that space, so it is open to view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the bathroom answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנינא מסורא's answer that the empty space is used as a bathroom.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bathroom requires privacy, and an open, unwalled space cannot provide it.

steps.title: It is a nighttime bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he uses the space as a bathroom only at night, when nobody can see.
steps.simpleTranslation: He makes it into a bathroom for nighttime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the privacy problem by saying the space is a bathroom used only at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night the darkness gives the privacy that a wall would normally give. So the open space can still be a proper bathroom, and the bathroom answer from step 5 stays in place.

phrases.english: That he makes it into a bathroom for nighttime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the privacy challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the bathroom is limited to nighttime use.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bathroom is used at any time, so the open space would not be private.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is used only at night, when darkness provides privacy.

steps.title: Even at night a person must be modest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the nighttime answer with a ברייתא teaching that a modest person behaves at night the same way he behaves during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Master said: Who is a modest person? One who relieves himself at night in the place where he relieves himself by day. And even though we explained this as talking about the same manner of behavior and not the same place, we still learn that he must act modestly even at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the nighttime answer. It quotes a ברייתא that shows a person must keep צניעות even at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a צנוע relieves himself at night just as he does by day. The גמרא admits this was explained as being about behavior, how carefully he uncovers himself, and not about location. Either way, it shows that darkness does not cancel the duty of modesty, so a nighttime bathroom in an open space is still a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: We explained it as referring to

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not using the ברייתא to say he must go to the same place at night. It admits the ברייתא is about acting in the same modest manner. The point it takes is only that modesty is still required at night.

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say: Who is a modest person?
One who relieves himself at night in the place where he relieved himself by day,
And even though we explained it as meaning "in the same manner,"
phrases.notes: He means: we explained the ברייתא as being about how modestly he behaves, not about which spot he uses.

phrases.english: Still, he needs to act with modesty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the nighttime-bathroom answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a nighttime bathroom needs no privacy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that the duty of modesty applies at night too, so darkness alone is not enough.

steps.title: It is a bathroom for children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the space is used as a bathroom for small children.
steps.simpleTranslation: He makes it into a bathroom for children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the modesty problem: the open space is a bathroom for little children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small children are not held to the same rules of צניעות as adults. So an open bathroom is fine for them, and the space still is not used in a way that helps the עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: That he makes it a bathroom for children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the modesty challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the bathroom is for children, who are not bound by adult modesty rules.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bathroom is for adults, who must keep צניעות even at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is for children, so the lack of privacy is not a problem.

steps.title: Another answer: fencing off the space with thorns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a different answer to the original question: he fences the extra space with thorns and shrubs so it cannot be used at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another answer: he fences it in with thorns and shrubs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the original question from step 4 and offers a completely different answer, without the bathroom idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that pulling the wall back gives the עבודה זרה extra space. If he blocks that space with thorns and shrubs, nobody can walk there or use it, so the idol gains nothing. This answer avoids all the modesty problems of the bathroom answer.
steps.whatToRemember: Pulling the wall back must not give the עבודה זרה any benefit. The גמרא solves this either by making the space a bathroom (finally, one for children) or by blocking it off with thorns and shrubs.

phrases.english: Alternatively,
That he fences it in with thorns and shrubs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, דְּגָדַיר לֵיהּ בְּהִיזְמֵי וְהִיגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bathroom line of steps 5 to 9 and gives a separate answer to the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative practical solution: blocking the space so it cannot be used.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra open space would be usable and so would benefit the עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fenced with thorns and shrubs, the space is unusable, so the idol gains no benefit.

steps.title: The three kinds of houses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches three cases of a house connected to עבודה זרה, each with its own law.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three kinds of houses. A house built from the start for עבודה זרה is forbidden. If someone plastered or cemented a house for עבודה זרה and added something new, he removes what he added. If someone brought an idol into a house and took it out, the house is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: houses and עבודה זרה. It gives three cases, from fully forbidden to fully permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How involved the house is decides the law. Built for the idol: the whole house is forbidden. Only a new layer added for the idol: only that layer is forbidden. The idol was just inside for a time: nothing is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He cemented it, or decorated the plaster

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: built for עבודה זרה is forbidden; an added layer means remove only the layer; an idol brought in and taken out leaves the house permitted.

phrases.english: MISHNA: There are three kinds of houses —
A house that he built from the start for idol worship,
is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Forbidden means you may not get any benefit or use from it.

phrases.english: If he plastered it or cemented it for idol worship, and added something new —
he removes what he added.
If he brought an idol into it and then took it out —
the house is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Built for עבודה זרה: forbidden. An added layer for עבודה זרה: remove the addition. An idol brought in and removed: permitted.

steps.title: Bowing to a house makes it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person who bows to a house makes it forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Someone who bows down to a house has made it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רב that goes beyond the משנה: bowing to an ordinary house makes it forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only spoke of a house built for עבודה זרה. רב says even a regular house becomes forbidden if someone worships it by bowing to it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav said:
One who bows to a house has made it forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new way, not stated in the משנה, for a house to become forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bowing to a house makes it forbidden.

steps.title: What רב must hold, and a challenge from the משנה's word 'built'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא works out that רב treats something built from loose materials as still loose, then challenges him from the משנה, which only mentions building.
steps.simpleTranslation: So רב must hold that something that was loose and later attached to the ground counts as loose. But our משנה says 'he built it,' which suggests only building forbids the house.
steps.whatsHappening: First the גמרא explains the idea behind רב's ruling. Then it challenges him from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things attached to the ground cannot become forbidden through worship, but loose things can. A house is attached, yet it was made of loose stones, so רב must treat it as loose. The challenge: the משנה forbids a house only when it was 'built' for עבודה זרה, so how can bowing alone forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: He attached it to the ground

steps.confusionAlert: The inference ('אלמא') is not an attack on רב. It only explains his reasoning. The real challenge begins at 'והאנן בנאו תנן'.

phrases.english: Evidently, he holds
that something detached that he later attached
is considered detached,
phrases.notes: A house is built from loose stones, so it can be forbidden like any loose object.

phrases.english: But we learned 'he built it' in the משנה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב's reasoning, then challenges it from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that bowing to a house forbids it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names building for עבודה זרה as what forbids a house. That suggests a house becomes forbidden only by being built for it, not by bowing.

steps.title: Two separate ways: building or bowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that building and bowing each forbid a house on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he built it for עבודה זרה, it is forbidden even if he never bowed to it. If he bowed to it, it is forbidden even if he did not build it for that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב: the משנה's case and רב's case are two separate ways for a house to become forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that building alone forbids, even without bowing. רב adds that bowing alone forbids, even without building for it. The משנה does not rule out bowing.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנָאוֹ — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה לוֹ,
phrases.english: If he built it, it is forbidden even if he did not bow to it;

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא בְּנָאוֹ.
phrases.english: if he bowed, it is forbidden even if he did not build it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנָאוֹ — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: two independent ways to forbid a house
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's word 'built' seemed to mean only building forbids a house.
steps.terutzMaskana: Building is one way and bowing is another. The משנה teaches one and רב teaches the other.

steps.title: Then there should be four houses, not three
steps.stepSummary: If bowing is a separate way, the משנה should have counted four kinds of houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, these 'three' houses are really four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. If bowing is its own case, why does the משנה say there are only three houses?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opens with a number, 'three houses.' A count usually means to be complete. Adding רב's bowing case makes four, so the count looks wrong.

phrases.english: If so,
these three are really four!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הָנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה — אַרְבָּעָה הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14 using the משנה's count.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that building and bowing are separate cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two separate forbidding cases plus the plastering case and the idol-brought-in case add up to four, but the משנה says three.

steps.title: Building and bowing count as one
steps.stepSummary: Building and bowing are cancelled the same way, so the משנה counts them as one kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since, for cancelling the forbidden status, building and bowing work the same, the משנה counts them as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the counting problem: the משנה groups houses by their law, and building and bowing share the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's three kinds are grouped by how the ban works and how it can be undone. A built house and a bowed-to house are cancelled the same way, so they fill one slot. The count of three stays correct, and רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelling the forbidden status of עבודה זרה

steps.whatToRemember: רב: bowing to a house forbids it, just as building it for עבודה זרה does. The משנה still says 'three' because building and bowing are cancelled the same way and count as one kind.

phrases.english: Since with regard to cancelling the forbidden status,

phrases.aramaic: בָּנָה וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה חַד קָא חָשֵׁיב לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: building and bowing are the same, it counts them as one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and closes this discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the משנה groups its cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two separate ways to forbid a house should be counted as two separate houses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה counts by the law of cancelling. Building and bowing share that law, so they count as one.

steps.title: The three kinds of stones
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three kinds of stones and their rules regarding עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three kinds of stones. A stone cut from the start to be a base for an idol is forbidden. A stone plastered or cemented for an idol: remove the plaster and cement, and the stone is permitted. A stone that an idol was set on and later removed is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Just as the earlier משנה listed three kinds of houses, this one lists three kinds of stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The level of connection to the idol decides the outcome. A stone shaped for the idol from the start is fully forbidden. Added plaster can be peeled off, and an idol that only stood on the stone leaves no lasting mark, so in those two cases the stone is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A platform or base that an idol stands on
He cut or hewed it out (from the quarry)
He plastered it and cemented it

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section of the גמרא is about the middle case, the plastered stone, and how it compares to the plastered house in the earlier משנה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There are three kinds of stones:
A stone that he cut from the start for a platform
phrases.notes: The platform here is the base an idol stands on.

phrases.english: is forbidden.
If he plastered it or cemented it for the sake of idol worship,
he removes what he plastered and cemented,
and it is permitted.
If he set up an idol on it and then removed it,
it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה, built in parallel to the earlier משנה of three houses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stone cut for an idol is forbidden. A plastered stone is permitted once the plaster is removed. A stone an idol stood on is permitted once the idol is removed.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the plaster must go into the stone itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says the plastered stone case applies only when the plaster was worked into the stone itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: This applies only when he plastered and cemented into the body of the stone itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי narrows the middle case of the משנה. The stone is affected only if the plaster went into the stone itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the plaster is just stuck onto the outside, the stone itself was never really involved, so it was never forbidden at all. Only when the stone itself was worked on does it need its plaster removed.

keyTerms.meaning: In the body of the stone itself

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Ami said:
And this is only when he plastered and cemented
into the body of the stone itself.
phrases.notes: He means the plaster was worked into the stone, not just smeared on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the second case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plastered stone is affected only if the plaster went into the stone itself.

steps.title: Challenge: a plastered house is forbidden even from outside plaster
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי, since the stone case is like the house case, and a house is forbidden even though plaster is only on its surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned the stone case as similar to the house case. And with a house, the plaster is not in the house itself, yet the house becomes forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אמי's limit using the earlier משנה about a house plastered for idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה places stones right next to houses, so they should follow the same rules. A plastered house is forbidden even though plaster seems to sit only on the outside of the walls. So outside plaster should affect a stone as well, against רבי אמי.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn it similar to a house?
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier משנה, where a house plastered for idol worship is forbidden.

phrases.english: And with a house, the plaster is not in its body,
and yet it becomes forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's limit.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's rule that the plaster must be in the stone itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stone is parallel to house, and a house is forbidden by surface plaster, so a stone should be too.

steps.title: Answer: in a house, plaster fills the gaps between bricks
steps.stepSummary: Plaster on a house also gets into the house itself, because it fills the spaces between the bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a house too, there is space between the bricks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the house case also involves plaster going into the structure itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plaster on a wall seeps into the gaps between the bricks, so it becomes part of the house. That makes the house just like a stone with plaster worked into it, and רבי אמי's rule stands.

phrases.english: With a house too,
there is space between the bricks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the house.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case so it fits the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: House plaster sits only on the outside surface.
steps.terutzMaskana: House plaster fills the gaps between bricks, so it is in the house itself.

steps.title: Challenge: what about a house plastered a second time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה should also cover a house that was already plastered and then plastered again for the idol, where the new layer never touches the bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Aren't we also dealing with a case where he plastered it, and then plastered it again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 20, that house plaster fills the gaps between the bricks. The next step answers this by reading רבי אמי's statement in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say which kind of plastering it means, so it should include a house that already had normal plaster and was then plastered again for idol worship. The second layer touches only the old plaster, not the gaps between the bricks, yet the house is still forbidden. So 'between the bricks' does not explain every case.

phrases.english: Aren't we dealing even
with a case where he plastered, and then plastered it again?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּשִׁייעַ, וַהֲדַר שַׁיְיעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that house plaster fills the gaps between bricks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the משנה does not specify, it covers a second layer of plaster that never reaches the bricks, and that house is still forbidden. So the gaps cannot be the full explanation.

steps.title: רבי אמי was really talking about making the stone permitted again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves רבי אמי's statement to the ביטול part of the משנה. Even if the plaster went into the stone itself, removing the added plaster makes the stone permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אמי's statement was said about ביטול, making the stone permitted again. Even if someone plastered or cemented into the stone itself, once he removes what he added, the stone is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenges in Steps 19 and 21 knocked down the first reading of רבי אמי, so the גמרא gives a new reading. His statement is about getting rid of the stone's forbidden status, not about when it becomes forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבי אמי seemed to limit when a plastered stone becomes forbidden: only when the plaster goes into the stone. Now his words are read as a leniency. Even in that stronger case, where the plaster is worked into the stone, removing the new addition is enough to permit it. This gets rid of the problem with the house, because רבי אמי is no longer setting a condition for the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: cancelling the forbidden status of something used for עבודה זרה
removed what he had newly added
it is fine; it is permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two halves of the משנה. Becoming forbidden comes from plastering the stone for the idol. Becoming permitted comes from removing that plaster. רבי אמי is now being read as speaking only about the second part.

phrases.english: Rather, when the statement of Rabbi Ami was said
it was said about cancelling the stone's forbidden status,
and even though he plastered or cemented
into the body of the stone itself,
when he removes what he added,
it is fine (permitted).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי אִתְּמַר דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי לְעִנְיַן בִּיטּוּל אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21 by moving רבי אמי's statement to a different part of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-assigning the statement to a different clause of the משנה (from becoming forbidden to becoming permitted)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי was limiting when a plastered stone becomes forbidden, and that conflicted with the house case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי was teaching that removing the added plaster permits the stone, even when the plaster was worked into the stone itself.

steps.title: Why רבי אמי needed to teach this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי אמי's חידוש. You might have thought plaster worked into the stone makes it like a stone carved for עבודה זרה, so the whole stone is forbidden. He teaches that removing the addition is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since he plastered or cemented into the stone itself, it is like a stone that was carved for עבודה זרה from the start, so the entire stone should be forbidden. רבי אמי teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new point רבי אמי is adding. It shows the mistaken idea we might have had without his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone carved for עבודה זרה from the start is fully forbidden. Removing something from it does not help. Plaster that soaks into the stone could have looked like that kind of change to the stone itself. רבי אמי teaches that it is still only an addition, so removing it permits the stone.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)
he teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading of רבי אמי: a stone plastered for עבודה זרה becomes permitted once the added plaster is removed. This is true even if the plaster went into the stone itself. It is not treated like a stone carved for עבודה זרה from the start.
steps.whyThisMatters: It draws the line between adding something to an object for an idol, which can be undone by removing the addition, and shaping the object itself for the idol, which forbids the whole thing.

phrases.english: For you might have said:
since he plastered or cemented
into the body of the stone,
it is like a stone that he carved from the start
phrases.notes: This is the first case in the משנה from Step 17, a stone carved for the idol, which is completely forbidden.

phrases.english: for idol worship,
and the whole stone should be forbidden,
he teaches us that it is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the חידוש of the new reading of רבי אמי given in Step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Plaster worked into a stone is still only an addition. Removing it permits the stone, unlike a stone carved for עבודה זרה from the start.
